conflict_synopsis.core_view: Receive AU 2Y versus pay CA 2Y to collect the 165bp common-date 2Y gap while housing bites in Australia and BoC energy risk is still only conditional; reject stretched AUDCAD and reject global long duration.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Australian housing/labor confirmation plus any BoC conversion of energy pass-through risk into tightening bias.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AU tightening channel fades while BoC energy risk is retired and the AU–CA 2Y differential no longer pays the AU receiver.

remit: positive carry and patient expressions across rates and FX unless a catalyst overwhelms it
stance_summary: Receive the Australian 2-year versus pay the Canadian 2-year. Verified: on the common 2026-09-16 date the CA−AU 2Y spread is −164.9bp, the packet’s largest available 2Y yield differential, while AUDCAD spot already sits at a 5-year extreme. Inference: housing is biting in Australia and BoC energy pass-through is still only a conditional tightening trigger, so the remaining AU–CA discrepancy lives in front-end rates, not in stretched AUDCAD. Unknown: forwards, OIS paths, and tickets. Global long-duration is rejected because the post-Fed tightening/energy catalyst overwhelms positive carry there; NZ rates RV is unavailable.

catalysts: Further Australian housing, credit, or labor prints confirming the RBA channel is biting, allowing AU 2Y to ease from 5y extremes while still paying carry.
BoC communication or Canada CPI energy/core mix that converts the minutes’ pass-through risk into actual tightening bias, lifting CA 2Y versus AU.
Persistence of the global energy shock (Brent already extreme) that keeps G10 easing capped without forcing a net-long global-duration overlay.
evidence_refs: rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
rollup:Canada August inflation holds at 3%, core stays near 2%

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Duration-matched receive Australian 2-year sovereign versus pay Canadian 2-year sovereign (CA−AU 2Y). Common-date spread −164.9bp as of 2026-09-16; AU 2Y 4.999% (5y percentile 99.80) versus CA 2Y 3.27% on 2026-09-17 (5y percentile 58.59).
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates is the cleaner expression of the same AU–CA carry gap. AUDCAD has already paid the differential at a 5-year extreme, so chasing spot is late and fading it is negative-carry. The rates spread still has 5y-history cheapness in CA versus AU (CA−AU 2Y 5y percentile 10.50, z_5y −1.64) while CA 2Y itself is only 58.59 percentile on 5y history. NZ-involved rate RV is unavailable. Prefer rates when comparably clean; here rates is strictly cleaner.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Long AUDCAD: same 2Y differential of 164.9bp versus 60-day FX vol 4.93 (ratio 0.334), but ECB reference spot 0.9976 at 5y percentile 99.96 and z_5y 2.76.

trade.horizon: 1–3 months, patient; let 2Y differential carry fund timing slippage unless a catalyst overwhelms it
trade.invalidation: Mechanism fails if Australian housing and AU labor stop showing tightening-channel bite while Bank of Canada retires energy pass-through risk and core inflation stays near 2%, or if the AU–CA 2Y differential ceases to pay the receiver of AU. No unsourced price stop.
trade.mispricing: Verified: FX has already expressed AU versus CA (AUDCAD 5y percentile 99.96, z_5y 2.76) while CA−AU 2Y remains in the 10th percentile of 5y history and CA 2Y is only mid-pack on 5y (percentile 58.59) despite a 1y stretch (percentile 97.82, z_1y 2.46). Inference: the gap between a fully expressed high-carry FX cross and an only-moderately stretched 5y rate spread is the discrepancy; mean reversion of CA−AU 2Y toward less negative, and/or AU yields easing as housing bites, closes it with positive 2Y differential carry. Unknown: whether 1y-window unstretched CA−AU 2Y (percentile 51.39) means the 5y cheapness is a regime level rather than a tradeable gap. Do not treat the z-score as a target.
principal_risks: Canada labor is already cooler (employment −42k, wages +2.0% y/y); if that dominates energy, the pay-CA leg is wrong and the spread can stay wide.
Saudi Oman workaround and modest oil easing can retire the BoC pass-through catalyst even while shock-absorber headlines remain mixed.
Global tightening (Fed, BoJ 1.25%, BoE 6–3 hike dissent) can lift AU yields further despite housing, so the receive-AU leg is not a free hedge.
CA−AU 2Y is unstretched on the 1y window (percentile 51.39); 5y cheapness may be a regime, not a closing gap.
Carry screen is a 2Y yield differential over 60d FX vol, not forward carry, roll-down, or expected return; holding-period return is therefore only partly quantified.
AU yields are two sessions old versus CA; market-state is stale; NZ rates are unavailable; no positioning feed; no executable broker prices.
Empty paper books are not a constraint and invent no existing risk.
trade.structure: Duration-matched receive Australian 2-year government bonds versus pay Canadian 2-year government bonds (CA−AU 2Y). Research yields only; not a broker ticket and not a DV01-invented size.
trade.thesis: Causal question: after a global tightening impulse, is the AU–CA 2Y gap still a paid, patient holding-period expression, or has FX already absorbed it? Verified fact: AU 2Y is 4.999% as of 2026-09-16 (5y percentile 99.80, +39.1bp over 1m); CA 2Y is 3.27% as of 2026-09-17 (5y percentile 58.59, 1y percentile 97.82, +31bp over 1m, −8bp on 1d); common-date CA−AU 2Y is −164.9bp (5y percentile 10.50, z_5y −1.64; 1y percentile 51.39, 1y-window z about −0.41). The opportunity monitor flags that 164.9bp AUD–CAD 2Y differential as the largest available carry screen, explicitly not forward carry, funding, roll-down, or expected return. Australian housing evidence shows the RBA channel biting (NSW stamp-duty receipts −24% y/y, volumes −18%, Sydney and Melbourne values more than 7% from peak); AU labor is softer (unemployment 4.5%, employment −15.8k). BoC held 2.25% but judged fuel-inflation pass-through risk higher; Canada August headline CPI held at 3.0% with CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%; CA Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q while August employment was −42k and wage growth cooler. Brent was 130.8 USD/bbl as of 2026-09-15 (1y-window percentile 99.60). Desk synthesis: the energy shock constrains the global easing impulse and keeps term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer. Inference: receiving stretched AU front-end versus paying still-cheap-on-5y CA front-end isolates local divergence without owning global duration, and the 2Y yield gap pays the holder while housing transmission and conditional BoC energy risk play out. Unknown: implied OIS hike counts, true forward points, roll-down, funding, positioning, and executable levels.
why_now: Fed has already delivered the widely priced 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%; the residual question is relative, not whether US tightening occurred.
Australian housing and softer AU labor are current evidence that the high AU 2Y is starting to do work, which is when receiving that yield becomes a paid wait rather than a fight with the RBA.
BoC minutes plus Brent at a 1y extreme keep CA energy pass-through as a live conditional, while core Canada is still near 2%, so paying CA is relative-value not a committed hike call.
AUDCAD is already at a 5-year extreme, so the same view in spot is late; the rates RV is the unexpressed remainder.
